_why: `layout_model.nim` beside this file is a VERBATIM copy of CodeTracer's
`src/frontend/headless_app/layout_model.nim`. It is vendored rather than
imported for one reason: the client's build is hermetic. `flake.nix` pins
isonim, nim-everywhere and the design system and nothing else, so
`nix build .#default` has no CodeTracer checkout on the Nim path at all.
Adding one so that a 542-line, stdlib-only, renderer-free data structure
could be imported would put the whole CodeTracer tree into the static
site's closure to gain a tree of five constructors.
Vendoring is also what the module itself asks for. Its own header says the
model lives on the CONSUMER side of the SDK boundary because 'arranging
panes is the embedder's job' — it is deliberately NOT exported through
`codetracer_embed.nim`, so there is no facade route to it and reaching into
`headless_app/` from here would be exactly the internal-module import that
M8a's `test_thin_slice_uses_only_the_sdk_facade` forbids.
What keeps a copy honest is `ci/test/layout-model-vendor.sh`:
A. the bytes here still hash to `sha256` below (no local edits), and
B. against a real CodeTracer checkout, a probe imports BOTH modules and
compares `defaultReplayLayout()`, `allPanes`, `visiblePanes` and
`validate` — so a structural change upstream fails here rather than
leaving BlockTracer arranging panes to a shape nobody else has.
NOTE ON THE COMMIT. This is not `ci/embed-sdk-pin.env`'s `CODETRACER_REF`,
and the difference is deliberate: that pin names the commit whose
`src/frontend/viewmodel/` tree IS the Embed SDK, and `headless_app/` is not
in that tree. At the Embed SDK pin (86719698) this module still called the
five-pane set `BlockTracerPanes`; upstream has since renamed it to
`ReplayCorePanes` precisely because an exported symbol naming one embedder
is the boundary eroding from the inside. Vendoring the pre-rename name into
that same embedder would reintroduce the smell, so this tracks the module's
own mainline and records which commit it came from.
